name: ChauffeurPilot Booking
author: tahiramjad

sections.description:
ChauffeurPilot Booking puts your chauffeur, limousine or airport transfer booking form on your WordPress site. Customers enter their journey, see a fixed price for each vehicle class, and book and pay online. Every booking lands in your ChauffeurPilot dashboard, ready to assign to a driver.

The plugin is the WordPress connector for ChauffeurPilot, a booking and dispatch platform for chauffeur companies. You need a ChauffeurPilot account to use it. See pricing for current plans.

What your customers get

  • Instant fixed prices. Pick-up, drop-off, date and time in, a price for each vehicle class out.
  • One way or by the hour. Both journey types in the same form.
  • Address search and route map. Address autocomplete with a map preview of the route.
  • Airport pick-ups. A flight number field appears when the pick-up is an airport.
  • Online payment. Card payments are handled by Stripe inside the booking form.
  • Works on mobile. The form resizes to fit the page and the screen.

What you get in WordPress

  • Gutenberg block. Add the “ChauffeurPilot Booking” block to any page or post.
  • Shortcode. Use [chaubo_booking] in any editor, widget or page builder.
  • Elementor widget. Optional. Same options as the block.
  • Two form sizes. A compact search form for your homepage and the full booking form for your booking page. The compact form passes the journey details on to the full form.
  • Three placements. Inline, full width, or a button that opens the form in a popup.
  • Test and Live modes. Try the form on a staging or local site before you take real bookings.
  • Setup checklist. The settings page shows what is connected and what is still missing.

How it works

  1. You build and style your booking form in the ChauffeurPilot dashboard, and set your vehicles and prices there.
  2. The plugin shows that published form on your WordPress pages inside a secure iframe.
  3. Changes you publish in ChauffeurPilot appear on your site without touching WordPress again.

Pricing, vehicles, payments, drivers and bookings are all managed in ChauffeurPilot. The plugin itself stores only three settings: your organization slug, the Test or Live choice, and the address of your booking page.

Who it is for

Chauffeur and executive car companies, limousine services, airport transfer operators, and hotels or agencies that take chauffeur bookings on a WordPress site.

Documentation and support

  • WordPress setup guide
  • Installation walkthrough
  • Homepage search form with a separate booking page
  • Elementor widget
  • Troubleshooting

For help with the plugin, use the support forum on this page. For help with your ChauffeurPilot account, bookings or payments, contact ChauffeurPilot through chauffeurpilot.com.

External services

This plugin connects your site to the ChauffeurPilot service. It cannot show a booking form without it.

What is loaded and when. On every page where you place the block, shortcode or widget, the visitor’s browser opens an iframe from a ChauffeurPilot server:

  • Live mode: https://embed.chauffeurpilot.com
  • Test mode: https://embed-staging.chauffeurpilot.com

The small loader script (embed.js) is bundled with the plugin and served from your own site. No script is loaded from a remote server.

What is sent. The iframe address contains your organization slug, the Test or Live choice, the address of the page the form is on, and, when a visitor uses the compact search form, the journey details they typed (pick-up, drop-off, date, time, flight number, passengers). Everything the visitor enters in the booking form itself, including contact and payment details, is sent by their browser directly to ChauffeurPilot and its payment provider Stripe. None of it passes through or is stored in WordPress.

Nothing is sent on pages that do not contain a booking form, and the plugin does not track visitors.

The service is provided by ChauffeurPilot: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. More detail: Privacy and data.
sections.installation:
Before you start

Create a ChauffeurPilot account at chauffeurpilot.com, add at least one vehicle class with prices, and publish your booking form.

Install the plugin

  1. In WordPress go to Plugins > Add New, search for “ChauffeurPilot Booking”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. You are taken to Settings > ChauffeurPilot.

Connect your account

  1. In ChauffeurPilot open Connect and copy your organization slug.
  2. Paste it into Organization slug in the plugin settings.
  3. Choose Live for a public website. Choose Test for a staging site.
  4. Click Save Changes.
  5. Copy the Parent origin shown in the Setup status box and add it in ChauffeurPilot under Connect > Channels > Embed sites. This tells ChauffeurPilot that your website is allowed to show your form.

Add the form to a page

  • Block editor: add the ChauffeurPilot Booking block.
  • Shortcode: add [chaubo_booking].
  • Elementor: drag in the ChauffeurPilot Booking widget.

Publish the page and open it. Your booking form is live.

Optional: search form on the homepage

  1. Create a page for the full form, for example /book/, and add the block with Mode set to Full.
  2. Enter that page address in Default full form page URL in the plugin settings.
  3. On your homepage add the block with Mode set to Lite.

Visitors start their journey on the homepage and finish the booking on your booking page.
sections.faq:
Do I need a ChauffeurPilot account?

Yes. The plugin shows the booking form you create in ChauffeurPilot. Without an account there is no form to show.

Is the plugin free?

The plugin is free. ChauffeurPilot is a paid service with its own plans. See pricing.

Where do I set prices, vehicles and the look of the form?

In the ChauffeurPilot dashboard. The plugin only decides where the form appears on your site.

Does WordPress handle payments or store card details?

No. Payment happens inside the booking form, which runs on ChauffeurPilot servers and uses Stripe. Card details never reach your WordPress site. You connect your Stripe account in ChauffeurPilot.

What is the difference between Test and Live?

Live shows your real form and takes real bookings. Use it on your public website.

Test uses a separate staging form so you can try things safely. The plugin switches to Test by itself on local and development sites (for example localhost or .local addresses), because those cannot take real bookings.

The form does not appear. What should I check?

  1. The organization slug in Settings > ChauffeurPilot matches the one in ChauffeurPilot exactly.
  2. The environment is Live on a public website.
  3. Your site address is added under Connect > Channels > Embed sites in ChauffeurPilot.
  4. Your booking form is published in ChauffeurPilot.
  5. No security plugin or Content Security Policy is blocking iframes from embed.chauffeurpilot.com.

More in the troubleshooting guide.

What are the shortcode options?

[chaubo_booking] works with no options. You can add:

  • mode – lite, full or auto
  • placement – inline, full_width or modal
  • button_label – text of the button when placement is modal
  • min_height – for example 640px
  • full_form_url – booking page address used by the lite form
  • org – a different organization slug for this one form

Example: [chaubo_booking mode="lite" min_height="640px"]

The older shortcode [chauffeurpilot_booking] still works.

Can I put the form in a popup?

Yes. Set Placement to Modal in the block or widget, or use [chaubo_booking placement="modal" button_label="Book a ride"].

Do I need Elementor?

No. The block and the shortcode work without it.

Does it work with my theme and page builder?

The block works with any block theme or classic theme. The shortcode works anywhere shortcodes are supported, which covers most page builders.

Can I use more than one form on a site?

Yes. Add the block or shortcode to as many pages as you like. Use the org option if a page should show the form of a different organization.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

The plugin deletes its own settings. Your ChauffeurPilot account, bookings and customers are not affected.
sections.changelog:
1.0.6

  • Documentation: rewritten plugin description, installation guide and FAQ.
  • New directory screenshots taken from a real WordPress site, and a new banner.
  • No functional changes. Safe to update.

1.0.5

  • Package slug alignment: distributable folder and main file are chauffeurpilot/chauffeurpilot.php.
  • Settings UI documents preferred shortcode [chaubo_booking] and legacy alias [chauffeurpilot_booking].
  • CSS custom properties renamed from --cp-* to --chaubo-*.
  • One-time migration copies legacy cp_booking_options into chaubo_options when the new option is empty.
  • Copy cleanup for WordPress.org review (no em dashes in strings or docs).

1.0.4

  • WordPress.org review: unique chaubo_ / CHAUBO_ prefixes for classes, functions, options, handles, and hooks.
  • Text domain set to plugin slug chauffeurpilot.
  • Contributors list uses WordPress.org username tahiramjad.
  • Preferred shortcode [chaubo_booking] (legacy [chauffeurpilot_booking] still works).

1.0.1

  • Professional settings Setup status: parent origin copy, effective iframe host, Test/Live badge, Connect deep links.
  • Gutenberg and Elementor: Mode & handoff, Placement & height, Advanced panels with clearer guidance.
  • Docs aligned: local embed.js loader + iframe on ChauffeurPilot hosts (not CDN script).

1.0.0

  • Initial public release: Gutenberg block, shortcode, Elementor widget, Test/Live environments, lite/full handoff, modal placement.
